paragraphs.text: This area has 18 documented events; of the 12 told here, all but the 1900 battle and siege, the May Fourth Movement and the 1989 protests are approximately placed.
In 1900 Boxers and Qing Dynasty troops besieged the foreign legations in Peking for 55 days, until the Eight-Nation Alliance relieved the siege.
Only the Treaty of Peking's name and year, 1905, are documented here.
Puyi, the last Qing emperor, was born here in 1906, approximately placed.
In 1917 Zhang Xun's army seized Beijing and reinstalled Puyi, a restoration Republican troops reversed within two weeks.
On May 4, 1919, students protested at Tiananmen, beginning the May Fourth Movement.
Feng Yuxiang staged the Beijing Coup in 1924, students in Beiping demanded resistance to Japanese aggression in 1935, and in 1937 battles near Beiping and Tianjin ended in a Japanese victory.
Xi Jinping was born here in 1953, Ai Weiwei in 1957, and Jet Li in 1963, all approximately placed.

Red August, beginning in August 1966 during the Cultural Revolution, was a period of political violence and massacres in Beijing; official statistics published in 1980 said Red Guards killed 1,772, those of November 1985 gave 10,275 deaths.
In April 1976, after Zhou Enlai's death, crowds protested at Tiananmen Square, and that October a bloodless coup arrested the Gang of Four.
Zhang Ziyi was born here in 1979, approximately placed.
From 15 April to 4 June 1989, students and workers protested in Tiananmen Square, until government troops occupied it in the Tiananmen Square massacre.
